title: R' Yudan of Magdalaya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: [Taanit, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.1.3.4), relates that Rabbi Yosi bar Yaakov went up to visit Rabbi Yudan of Magdalaya. While he was there, rain fell, and he heard a voice saying: “A thousand thousands—we are obliged to give thanks.” He asked, “Where did you get this?” He answered, “This is how Rabbi Simon, my teacher, blesses.” The same appears in Berakhot, chapter 9. [Bereshit Rabbah 13:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.13.15) gives the name as Rabbi Yehudah of Magdalah.[^1]

notes.text: עד דהוה תמן means “while he was there,” not “until”; קליה refers to a voice, rather than necessarily the sound of the rain. Hyman abridges the blessing with a dash; the missing words of the longer primary blessing are not inserted. The second רבי after Simon means “my teacher” in this exchange. The speaker pronouns are retained without adding a new historical identity. The Berakhot locator פ״ט סה״ב remains unconverted and unchecked. פ״יג-טו is chapter 13, section 15. The Yehudah of Magdalah variant remains distinct from Yudan of Magdalaya. The terminal source comma does not license an invented continuation.

The supplied heading abbreviates its title and therefore remains R'. Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit 1:3:4, explicitly calls the visitor Rabbi Yosi bar Yaakov, the visited scholar Rabbi Yudan, and the teacher Rabbi Simon in this same rain-blessing account. The named *Midrash Rabbah -- TE* paragraph at Bereshit Rabbah 13:15 explicitly uses Rabbi Yehudah of Magdalah. These titles apply to the corresponding narrative occurrences; they do not harmonize the two name forms or establish a global identity.
